subject: is the model block in stan for the priors and likelihood?

messages.author: c53f37de2fa27727
messages.subject: is the model block in stan for the priors and likelihood?
parts:
Hi all,
I want to double check two things:
1) the model block in stan is for inputting the prior and likelihood models, not the posterior pdf. correct?

2) the examples given in stan user guide all involve the use of standard distributions for the models. My case involves a non standard likelihood model, which is formed by the product of two multivariate gaussian pdfs and two random vectors from gamma distribution, is the way to formulate such model is to direct such that I simply multiply the guassian distributions and random vectors together and consider them as the model?

Thanks in advance

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] is the model block in stan for the priors and likelihood?
parts:
> On May 10, 2017, at 10:38 AM, Mohammed Effat <mbef...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hi all,
> I want to double check two things:
> 1) the model block in stan is for inputting the prior and likelihood models, not the posterior pdf. correct?

Stan specifies a density up to a constant---it doesn't even have
to be a Bayesian posterior. If you code the log likelihood plus
log prior, that's equal to the log posterior up to an additive
constant. So there's no difference.

> 2) the examples given in stan user guide all involve the use of standard distributions for the models. My case involves a non standard likelihood model, which is formed by the product of two multivariate gaussian pdfs and two random vectors from gamma distribution, is the way to formulate such model is to direct such that I simply multiply the guassian distributions and random vectors together and consider them as the model?

You need to define the log density up to an additive constant.
Multiplying two Gaussians would require normalization. If you
write the density down, we can help.

- Bob

P.S. We're shuttering this list and moving to: http://discourse.mc-stan.org

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] is the model block in stan for the priors and likelihood?
parts:
You can just literally code all of that symbol-for-symbol in Stan.
It would be more efficient to use our normal distributions rather than
trying to write some of this out by hand (but be careful, because
we use the scale rather than variance or precision parameterizations).

Is there some part of it you can't figure out? I don't have the time
to go over a page of math and a page of Stan code and try to line them
up.

- Bob
